Home/How we work

One accountable engineer, a clear scope, and working software early.

There is no account manager and no offshore ticket queue. The person you talk to in the first call is the person who designs, builds and supports the system.

Process

Four steps, every project.

  1. 01

    Discover

    We map the workflow as it actually runs: who touches it, which systems, where the re-keying and waiting happen.

  2. 02

    Design

    We decide where automation and AI pay for themselves and where they do not. You get a written scope before any build starts.

  3. 03

    Build and deploy

    You see working software early, on your own documents and data, and your team tests it before it goes live.

  4. 04

    Operate and iterate

    After launch you keep a direct line to the engineer who built it, for fixes, changes and the next workflow.

Engagements

Start small. Go further if it earns it.

Every engagement is scoped to your workflow and systems, so we do not publish a price list. You see a written scope and quote before any build work starts.

  1. 01

    Workflow audit

    A short, contained first step. We map one workflow and its systems, rank the automation opportunities, and write up scope and data handling so your team can decide with facts.

    Where most firms start

  2. 02

    Targeted build

    One workflow, automated end to end. For example: rent roll to model, a borrower document portal, or LP onboarding.

    Typically live in weeks

  3. 03

    Operating system

    Several connected workflows, the integrations between your systems, a portal and a review queue, delivered in stages.

    Staged delivery

  4. 04

    Operate and iterate

    Ongoing support for what we built: fixes, changes, monitoring of extraction quality, and new workflows as you find them.

    After launch

The workflow audit

What you get from an audit.

A contained first step for firms that want facts before committing to a build.

  1. A map of the workflow as it really runs

    Who touches it, in which systems, and where the re-keying and waiting are.

  2. A systems and data-flow inventory

    What can be reached by API, what needs an export, and where the records of truth live.

  3. Ranked automation opportunities

    The few changes worth making, in order, each with a scope you can act on.

  4. A data-handling note for your compliance or security team

    How data would move, where it would live and who could see it.

Not sure where to start? Start with a workflow audit.

We map one workflow and the systems around it, rank the automation opportunities, and write up scope and data handling. You decide what, if anything, to build.
